name: The Manual Everyone Wants
summary: Half a scroll surfaces at an inn or out of a grave-robber's bundle, and every school that ever claimed descent from its author converges on the road at once — because the argument is not really about the pages, it is about whose lineage is the legitimate one. Blood is spent over paper. Whoever walks away holding it finds that the text was written for a body trained the way its author's students were trained, and reading it is not the same as owning it.

roles.label: the one who takes it
constraints: lacks the foundation the text assumes

roles.label: the wider martial world
constraints: will judge how it was taken

beats.label: The manual surfaces
beats.intent: word of the treatise reaches the martial world

beats.label: Everyone converges
beats.intent: factions with competing claims arrive at the same place

beats.label: Blood over paper
beats.intent: the contest is settled by force at a cost out of proportion to the prize

beats.label: Holding is not mastering
beats.intent: the winner finds the text unusable without what it presumes

preconditions.text: a martial world in which a technique confers real standing

effects.text: the holder is now a target rather than a possessor
the true prerequisite for the technique has become the new problem

examples.text: Eleven men died for the second half of it, and the man who walked out with it could not read the hand it was written in.

name: The Debt the Code Demands
summary: A stranger on the road is helped without calculation — a bowl of rice shared at an inn, a wound bound, a name spoken for before a magistrate — and the code of the rivers-and-lakes binds the HELPER, not the helped: having once stood for this person, they may not now stand aside. The claim is called in at the worst possible hour, and it is paid in reputation among strangers who will retell the choice at every inn from here to the provincial border.

roles.label: the one who helped without calculating
constraints: acted before knowing who it was

roles.label: the one helped
constraints: turns out to be costly to be owed by

beats.label: A stranger on the road is helped
beats.intent: rice is shared or a name is spoken for, before anyone knows whose it is

beats.label: The code of the rivers-and-lakes binds the helper
beats.intent: having once stood for this person, the helper may not stand aside

beats.label: The claim comes at the worst hour
beats.intent: standing by the stranger now costs the helper their own interest

beats.label: Paid in reputation, in front of strangers
beats.intent: the choice is made where travellers will carry it to every inn on the road

preconditions.text: a martial world where reputation is enforceable currency

effects.text: the helper's standing in the jianghu is fixed by the choice
a concrete interest has been surrendered or a code has been broken

examples.text: He had shared his rice with a beggar in the rain, and the beggar came back in silks with an escort, at exactly the wrong moment.

name: A Grudge Older Than the Holder
summary: A feud is handed down with the sword — two houses, two schools, two families who have killed each other's people for longer than anyone alive can properly account for. Forced to take a side, the inheritor goes looking for the original wrong and finds it either smaller than the killing warranted or already avenged, and must then choose between the cycle and the truth.

roles.label: the one who inherits the grudge
constraints: did not choose the side they were born to

roles.label: the original wrong
constraints: is smaller or older than the feud requires

roles.label: those who keep the feud alive
constraints: believe they are keeping faith with the dead

beats.label: The grudge is handed down
beats.intent: a feud is inherited along with position and blade

beats.label: Forced to take a side
beats.intent: an incident makes neutrality impossible

beats.label: The original wrong is found
beats.intent: the founding grievance is traced and turns out not to justify the ledger

beats.label: Continue the cycle or break it
beats.intent: the inheritor chooses between the dead and the living

preconditions.text: an old enmity, live again, whose origin nobody alive witnessed

effects.text: the feud is either renewed with full knowledge or publicly repudiated
the inheritor is estranged from one side of their own house

examples.text: Four generations of dead men, and at the bottom of it a dispute over a well that had run dry before any of them were born.

name: An Insult in a Public House
summary: A slight is offered in a room full of people who will carry the story — a name mocked, a school insulted, a cup knocked over deliberately. Restraint is tested in front of witnesses, one brief exchange settles it, and the account of what happened travels faster and further than either party intended.

roles.label: the one who offers the slight
the room that will retell it

beats.label: The slight is offered
beats.intent: an insult is made where it cannot be ignored privately

beats.label: Restraint is tested
beats.intent: the insulted party weighs what answering will cost

beats.label: One exchange settles it
beats.intent: a single brief demonstration ends the question

beats.label: The story travels
beats.intent: the account spreads and alters both reputations

preconditions.text: a public setting where reputation is made and unmade by report

effects.text: both parties' standing has shifted by report rather than by outcome
someone in the room now knows a capability that was not advertised

examples.text: The cup did not fall. Nobody in the room could say afterwards which of them had moved, only that the wine had not spilled.

name: The Method No One Practises Any More
summary: A school's proscribed manual — the kind the righteous sects burned copies of and still whisper about — is offered by someone who does not lie about what it does. It works exactly as promised. What it charges is not measured in rank: the body changes in ways other practitioners can read across a room, the orthodox schools that trained them disown the name, and the practitioner ends up belonging to the demonic side of a line they never meant to cross.

roles.label: the one at the wall
constraints: has genuinely exhausted the orthodox route

roles.label: the one who offers it
constraints: does not lie about the effect, only omits the price

beats.label: The school's own way runs out
beats.intent: what the master taught stops being enough for what is coming

beats.label: A proscribed manual is offered
beats.intent: someone honest about its effects puts the burned book in reach

beats.label: It is practised in secret
beats.intent: the demonic method is learned and delivers exactly what was promised

beats.label: The body reads it before words do
beats.intent: the change becomes legible to other practitioners and the orthodox schools disown the name

preconditions.text: a practitioner blocked by a wall the orthodox path cannot pass

effects.text: capability has genuinely increased and cannot be given back
a cost is now accruing that others can eventually see

examples.text: It did everything the old man said it would. It was two winters before anyone remarked that he no longer felt the cold.

name: Two Strangers of Matching Skill
summary: Two people who owe each other nothing exchange blows or words as a test rather than a quarrel, and each finds in the other the first opponent in years who does not have to be handled gently. Recognition arrives before names do, and the bond formed over wine afterwards will outlast most of the loyalties either of them was born into.

roles.label: the loyalties they were born into

beats.label: Two strangers meet
beats.intent: an encounter between parties who owe each other nothing

beats.label: An exchange without malice
beats.intent: skill is measured as a test rather than a quarrel

beats.label: Recognition before names
beats.intent: each finds the first equal they have met in years

beats.label: Sworn over wine
beats.intent: a bond is made that cuts across existing loyalties

preconditions.text: two parties of comparable skill and no prior obligation, each having seen in the other a capability that was not advertised

effects.text: a loyalty now exists that does not run along faction lines
both have a claim on the other that their own houses did not sanction

examples.text: Neither of them asked the other's name until the third cup, and by then it hardly mattered what the answer was.

name: The Cargo That Must Arrive
summary: Something must be moved from here to there — a chest, a witness, a bride, a coffin — along a road that everyone with an interest already knows about. The ambush is not a surprise but a schedule, and delivery is achieved by paying in exactly the coin the escort could least afford to spend.

beats.label: The charge is accepted
beats.intent: responsibility for safe delivery is given and taken

beats.label: The road is already known
beats.intent: it becomes clear the route was compromised before departure

beats.label: The ambush on schedule
beats.intent: the attack comes where and when it was always going to

beats.label: Delivered at cost
beats.intent: the charge arrives, paid for with something the escort valued more

preconditions.text: a charge whose route and value are known to interested parties

effects.text: the word given has been kept and something else has been lost
who leaked the route is now an open question

examples.text: They knew which ford, and roughly which hour, and the only thing left to decide was what he was willing to leave on the bank.

name: The One Who Put the Blade Down
summary: Someone who swore off the martial world is living quietly under another name when the past arrives at the door — an old enemy, a former student, a debt with legs. The vow is broken not for glory but because the alternative is worse, and the jianghu recognises the hand within days of it being raised.

roles.label: the one who put it down
the world that recognises the hand

beats.label: The quiet life
beats.intent: a former practitioner lives unrecognised and content

beats.label: The past at the door
beats.intent: something from before arrives that cannot be turned away

beats.label: The vow breaks
beats.intent: the blade is taken up because the alternative is worse

beats.label: The jianghu recognises the hand
beats.intent: the technique is identified and the quiet life ends

preconditions.text: a renounced past that others can still identify by technique

effects.text: an old enmity that long outlived its origin is live again, and knows where they are
the assumed identity no longer protects them

examples.text: He had been a ferryman for nine years, and it took one evening and one stroke for three provinces to learn he was not.
